title: The inclusions $\underline E\to\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$
statement:
For a finite subextension $E$ of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$, let
$j_E\colon\underline E\to\underline{\Qlb}$ be the morphism of condensed rings
([def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring], [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]) given by

$$
C(S,E)\ni a\longmapsto\bigl(S\xrightarrow{a}E\subseteq\Qlb\bigr)\in\underline{\Qlb}(S),
$$

viewed as a morphism of the underlying ring objects ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]). For
$E\subseteq F$, these maps satisfy $j_F\circ\iota_{E,F}=j_E$, with $\iota_{E,F}$ as in
[def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map].

proof.text: For a profinite set $S$, a section of $\underline E$ is a continuous map $a:S\to E$ by [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring]. Write $i_E:E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$ for the field inclusion. It is continuous because $E$ has the subspace topology; hence $i_E\circ a$ is continuous and its image lies in the finite subextension $E$. Thus $j_{E,S}(a):=i_E\circ a$ belongs to $\underline{\Qlb}(S)$ by [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. The domain operations and restrictions are pointwise operations and precomposition by [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and the target has these same formulas by [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For $a,b\in C(S,E)$ and $s\in S$, $i_E(a(s)+b(s))=i_E(a(s))+i_E(b(s))$ and $i_E(a(s)b(s))=i_E(a(s))i_E(b(s))$; also $i_E(0)=0$ and $i_E(1)=1$. These identities make $j_{E,S}$ a unital ring homomorphism. For $u:S'\to S$, $j_{E,S'}(a\circ u)=i_E\circ a\circ u=j_{E,S}(a)\circ u$, so the components are natural. They therefore define a morphism of sheaves of rings. Clause 3 of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] makes its underlying abelian-sheaf morphism a morphism of ring objects.

If $E\subseteq F$, the map [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map] is postcomposition with $E\subseteq F$. Therefore both $j_F\circ\iota_{E,F}$ and $j_E$ send every section $a:S\to E$ to the same composite $S\to E\subseteq\Qlb$, so the compatibility $j_F\circ\iota_{E,F}=j_E$ holds.
